"""Render statement lines as CSV."""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import io

from src.lines import Line


def format_amount(cents: int) -> str:
    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
    cents = abs(cents)
    return f"{sign}{cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"


def render(lines: list[Line]) -> str:
    # Quote any field containing a comma, quote or newline (RFC 4180) so every
    # row has exactly as many columns as the header, whatever the currency.
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(["account", "posted_on", "payee", "amount", "memo"])
    for line in lines:
        writer.writerow(
            [
                line.account,
                line.posted_on,
                line.payee,
                format_amount(line.amount_cents),
                line.memo,
            ]
        )
    return out.getvalue()
EOF
cat >> tests/test_statement.py <<'EOF'


def _parse(text):
    import csv
    import io

    return list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))


def test_usd_payee_with_comma_matches_the_header():
    text = export_statement(
        [Line("chk-100", "2024-06-02", "Smith, Jones LLP", 1250, "retainer", "USD")]
    )
    header, row = _parse(text)
    assert len(row) == len(header)
    assert row == ["chk-100", "2024-06-02", "Smith, Jones LLP", "12.50", "retainer"]


def test_eur_payee_and_memo_with_commas_are_preserved():
    text = export_statement(
        [Line("eur-1", "2024-06-02", "Müller, Schmidt", 100, "a, b", "EUR")]
    )
    header, row = _parse(text)
    assert row == ["eur-1", "2024-06-02", "Müller, Schmidt", "1.00", "a, b"]


def test_quotes_in_memo_round_trip():
    text = export_statement(
        [Line("chk-100", "2024-06-02", "Acme", 100, 'say "hi"', "USD")]
    )
    assert _parse(text)[1][4] == 'say "hi"'
EOF
